# Independent NVFP4 reference

`reference.json` is generated by `scripts/export_nvfp4_reference.py` using
NumPy and the synthetic Flint checkpoint in `test/flint/fixtures/tiny`.
It is independent of LifeAI's implementation.

```bash
python3 scripts/export_nvfp4_reference.py
julia -O1 --project=. test/test_nvfp4.jl
```

The oracle follows the documented NVIDIA [NVFP4 scale hierarchy](https://nvidia.github.io/TransformerEngine/features/low_precision_training/nvfp4/nvfp4.html)
and finite nearest-even [FP4 conversion](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-math-api/cuda_math_api/group__CUDA__MATH__FP4__MISC.html).
Its recipe is one-dimensional, rowwise block16 scaling. Payloads are E2M1,
scales are positive E4M3-FN, and the tensor-level decode scale is Float32.
The final input block is zero padded, and the first value occupies the low
nibble. This is a logical storage layout, without vendor GEMM scale swizzling.

Nine matrix cases cover all FP4 values, FP4 midpoint ties, all positive finite
FP8 scale encodings, FP8 midpoint ties, zero tensors, non-multiple-of-16 input
widths, subnormals and near-maximum Float32 values. Unsigned bit-pattern fields
preserve signed zeros even when a JSON parser normalizes decimal `-0.0`. The oracle also contains
53 quantized Flint projections plus full forward and greedy generation
references. Rounding is implemented through exhaustive codebook search rather
than LifeAI's exponent/threshold implementation.

Degenerate scale behavior is explicit: zero tensor scale is 1; a nonzero
underflowing global scale is clamped to the least positive Float32; an
unrepresentable upper product lowers the global scale by one Float32 ULP.
Blocks whose E4M3 scale rounds to zero contain canonical zero payloads.
Normalization uses `(weight / global_scale) / block_scale`, reconstruction
uses `(payload * block_scale) * global_scale` to avoid subnormal intermediate
scale underflow. The reference is not a claim of bitwise compatibility with
all ModelOpt/Transformer Engine recipes (which have optional scale clamps,
2D scaling, transforms or stochastic rounding).
